conventions.convention: Countable Choice is assumed for the compact spectral calculus and singular-system constructions; spaces may be real or complex over the same scalar field.
An admissible spectral index is bounded and nonnegative on zero together with the positive singular spectrum, with ψ(0)=0; source radii are strictly positive.
The source exponent ν is on |K|: |K|^ν=(K*K)^(ν/2), with ν>0.
The centered modulus uses one truth x, the constraint ||Kx||≤δ, and a class containing zero and contained in N(K)⊥; δ≥0 and the supremum may be infinite.
The two-truth modulus constrains ||K(x1−x2)||≤2δ; for the symmetric convex power source ball it equals twice the centered modulus.
Equality with the power-scale modulus bound is asserted at δ_j=ρs_j^(ν+1), rather than at every noise radius; finite rank and K=0 are treated separately.
Both diagonal examples explicitly use N={1,2,…}, real ℓ², operator norm one, and logarithmic index (1+log(1/t))^(−q).

load_bearing.statement: For ρ>0 define X_{ψ,ρ}(K):={ψ(|K|)w:w∈X, ||w||≤ρ}, where ψ is a bounded nonnegative spectral index with ψ(0)=0.
Assume Countable Choice. For compact K between real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field and ν,ρ>0, X_{ν,ρ}(K):={|K|^νw:||w||≤ρ}, where |K|^ν=(K*K)^(ν/2).

Assume Countable Choice. For compact K between real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field, a bounded nonnegative spectral index ψ with ψ(0)=0, and x=ψ(|K|)w, x∈N(K)⊥ and is the unique minimum-norm vector among z satisfying Kz=Kx.
Assume Countable Choice. Let K:X→Y be compact between real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field, ν>0, w∈X, and x=|K|^νw. Then ||x||≤||Kx||^(ν/(ν+1))||w||^(1/(ν+1)).
For compact K, 0∈M⊆N(K)⊥ and δ≥0, ε_K(M,δ):=sup{||x||:x∈M, ||Kx||≤δ}∈[0,+∞].

Under Countable Choice, for compact K between real or complex Hilbert spaces over the same scalar field and ν,ρ>0, ε_K(X_{ν,ρ}(K),δ)≤δ^(ν/(ν+1))ρ^(1/(ν+1)) for every δ≥0. Equality holds at δ_j=ρs_j^(ν+1), witnessed by ρs_j^νv_j for each positive singular value and unit right singular vector.

Under the stated compact Hilbert-space, Countable Choice and positive source-parameter assumptions, every deterministic reconstruction map A:Y→X satisfies E_δ(A)≥ε_K(X_{ν,ρ}(K),δ), hence so does its infimum over A; the two-truth modulus equals twice this centered modulus.

seams_checked.note: The required page supplies the compact Hilbert inverse model. Its actual Definition permits real or complex spaces over one field, compact K, and exact data Kx without injectivity or closed-range assumptions. Assigned consumers preserve this interface and obtain spectral and minimum-norm properties from separate suppliers.

This is a declared page prerequisite without a direct source-ball theorem citation in its two items. The veto retains its full-data-error-ball scope and explicitly excludes an inference against restricted solution/error classes; it does not overstate the source-ball lower bound.

The double-discrepancy theorem's F3 preserves |A|^ν=(A*A)^(ν/2). F8 quotes the interpolation inequality faithfully; Steps 2.1 and 2.2 establish the requisite source representations and source-vector bounds before applying it. Countable Choice and compact Hilbert hypotheses are explicit.

The ellipsoid-identification lemma uses the exact |K|^ν convention and the minimum-norm subspace. It derives weights s_j^(−ν), keeps Countable Choice, and explicitly restricts its statistical coordinate statement to real infinite-rank operators.

The ordered-filter Definition explicitly converts φ(T*T) to the singular-value index ψ(t)=φ(t²). Its spectral-range restriction makes ψ bounded there and ψ(0)=0. The oracle theorem's F4 uses this multiplier identification without confusing the two exponent conventions or importing an all-radius deterministic lower bound.
